configuration). Often managed by the application itself.
A resource that refers to some kind of data - a dataset, analysis, etc.
A resource that refers to something that monitors some other resource, such as a data-health system.
A system resource; infrastructure, nodes etc.
A resource that refers to some kind of logic, such as a transform, or contour dashboard.
A resource that refers to a request in the platform, such as a pull request or access request
A resource that refers to an Ontology object and its properties.
A list of resources that refer to Ontology objects and its properties and share the same common context.
A resource that refers to a selection or query over ontology data.

A resource that refers to a component that defines the Ontology, such as an ObjectType, LinkType or
the Ontology itself.

A resource that lies outside the system, such as an external client-id or identifier. Any 'floating' Identifier
types in categories will be classified as `external` by default.
Defines an explicit audit resource for review.

fields.docs: A description of what this context represents (eg. version, branch)

object.docs: Extra context surrounding a resource. This is a catch-all value, so could be a branch, version, etc.

fields.docs: The OntologyContext context to identify the resources.
Further context to further identify the resources.

object.docs: Represents the shared context across multiple resources.

union.docs:
A resource within a 'system', where a system constitutes potentially one or more nodes, environments, or
entities that host services.

fields.docs: A unique identifier for this token, if one exists.
The time at which this token expires, if known.
The user associated with this token, if known.

There are many different variants of token types, depending on the use-case and system. This type will
often determine the risk-profile of the token, so try to describe the token type that most accurately matches
the token you have.

object.docs:
A token represents a unit of permission that a user or service may have. Tokens typically grant some
degree of access to a system, after validation.
